<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/client/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/client/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type (route, 44 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a27e0235d5f7d674c8260b348c770762a9f969a0` — the merge of head `122847dc96a1e24adbc7f10012dbfdf8081c29a0` into base `9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a27e0235d5f7d674c8260b348c770762a9f969a0 && git checkout a27e0235d5f7d674c8260b348c770762a9f969a0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151 122847dc96a1e24adbc7f10012dbfdf8081c29a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151 && git merge --no-ff 122847dc96a1e24adbc7f10012dbfdf8081c29a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9a98a4675683a405aa911cd6c3e31f88bfe24151` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-b)

Head-sha: 3f16d0bcd2f9bb41afdbbdeeb6dc8b751cb3e904 · read 2026-11-21T08:28Z · full read of 141a826f..3f16d0bc (32 files, +1230/−154) against card #35424 items 6–9 and its acceptance list, the PR-b brief's three carried notes, and the before/after screenshots at 1280 and 375.

### 维护者速读

- 「全部文档」页现在有和其他页面一样的顶栏，写着「产品名 / 文档」，可以从这里回到任何应用。手册按应用分组，组名用启动器里的应用名；卡片上不再显示包 ID；副标题和篇数都按当前语言显示（「8 篇」）。
- 新增「搜索全部文档」：会搜标题、摘要和正文，结果里标出命中的词，点开后在文章自己的手册里阅读。只有第一次搜索时才去取全部正文，取的时候和列表走同一道权限关。
- 系统包的手册（比如「系统设置」）只列在对应应用下面。列表里没有这个应用的人（非管理员）就看不到这本。这是「列不列出来」的规则，谁能读仍由服务端决定。
- 建议补一处，不挡合并：没有单独写手册的包，搜索结果里的手册名还是旧的包名转写，中文界面下系统设置的文章会显示英文「Setup」，和卡片上的「系统设置」对不上。
- CI 全绿，可合并状态为 clean。

### Must-fix

None.

### Should-fix

- **S1 — a search hit names an implicit book by its package, not by its app.** `searchDocs` builds `bookLabel: book.label ?? book.name` (`docs-index.ts`). For an implicit book (`book.implicit`, a package with docs and no authored book) that label is `humanizePackageId(pkg)` (`book-nav.ts:432`). Meanwhile `groupBooksByApp` renames the same book's card to the owning app's label (`book.implicit ? { ...rest, label: owner.label }`). Example: Setup's docs. The card reads 「系统设置」, but a zh-CN search that hits a Setup article prints the book line as 「Setup」. That is an English word on the page, and it disagrees with the card one screen up. The card's acceptance asks for "zh-CN 下页面无英文句子、无包 ID". Fix: take the hit's book label from the listed cards, for example a `Map(book name → card label)` built from `groups` and passed to `searchDocs` (or have `searchDocs` take `groups`), with a unit case for an implicit book. (The reader page names the implicit book the same humanized way; that belongs to PR-a's surface and is not owed here.)

### Nits

- **N1** — `markTerms`/`snippetAround` take offsets from `toLocaleLowerCase()` text and slice the original. For the few characters whose lowercase changes length (e.g. `İ`), the marks shift by one. This is harmless for zh/en content; noted only.
- **N2** — The portal reader's column keeps `sticky top-12` (`DocPage.tsx:410`). That is right while the window scrolls under Home's sticky 48px bar. With the chat dock's rail open, `HomeLayout` bounds itself to `h-svh` and `main` scrolls in its own box, so the column would stop 48px below the box's top. That is an edge case, and Home's own pages share the frame.
- **N3** — On `/docs` the bar's search reads 「搜索应用、记录、页面…」 and the page's reads 「搜索全部文档」. They are distinct as the brief asked, and both appear in the screenshot. Two search fields on one page is a product call for later, not this PR.

### Checked

- **Item 6 (top bar).** `/docs` moves under the same pathless layout as `/home` (`RequireOrganization` + `ConsolePermissionsScope`, one `/auth/me/permissions` answer) as `DocsPortalRoute`. That is `DefaultHomeLayout variant="docs"` around the lazy `DocsLayout`, so the bar is up while the chunk loads. `AppHeader`'s `docs` variant is the home bar plus a `/ 文档` crumb linking to `/docs` (`app-bar-docs-crumb`). `DocShell`'s own portal strip and every `breadcrumb` prop are removed, with all six call sites updated. The old route already sat behind `ProtectedRoute`, which requires an organization by default, so the access requirement does not change. The 1280 screenshots show 「ObjectOS 预览版 / 文档」, the search, the bell, help and the avatar.
- **Item 7 (grouped by app).** `groupBooksByApp` puts a book under the first app whose navigation, including `areas[].navigation` at any depth, has a `doc` entry naming the book or one of its articles. Otherwise it goes under the first app of the book's package, and otherwise into 「其他文档」 last. Group names come from `useServedAppLabel` (the launcher's label) over `filterActiveApps`. The subtitle and counts are `help.*` keys in all 11 packs, with plural forms (`_one`/`_other`, es/fr/pt-BR `_many`, ar six forms); zh-Hant is regenerated (CI's generated check is green). The screenshot shows 「功能展示 / 示例手册 8 篇」 and 「系统设置 / 系统设置 1 篇」.
- **Item 8 (system packages).** The `subtitle` (package id line) is dropped from every card, and an implicit book takes its app's label. A `com.objectstack.*` book with no owning app in the caller's list is not listed, and its articles are kept out of search (`listedBooks`). The reading recorded in the changeset is "listed only where the caller's app list has its app" (Setup is served to administrators only), with the server's audience gate unchanged as the read gate. That is a fair reading of 「只给管理员看」.
- **Item 9 (search).** `useDocContents` asks `GET /meta/doc?include=content` once, when the first query is typed. It is sticky afterwards, re-asked only on a new adapter or a remount. The server already honours `include=content` (`meta-item-read-gate.ts:4641`) after its audience gate and locale collapse. `searchDocs` requires every word, ranks title over summary over body, strips mermaid, markup and link targets from bodies (`plainText`), and links each hit at `/docs/<its own book>/<doc>`. `?q=` is kept in the URL with `replace`. Results are rendered as React text with `<mark>` runs, never as HTML.
- **Carried notes.** (1) A reader URL whose book does not hold the doc redirects to the doc's own book once the doc is ready, guarded by `bookHoldsArticle` on the target. With no holding book, `ArticlePager` is not drawn (`resolvedBook && inBook`). Portal tests cover the redirect and its control. (2) The page search is labelled 「搜索全部文档」 (`help.searchAllDocs`), distinct from the column's 「搜索文档」, with a test. (3) `DocShell backLink={!docsNav}` is applied. `homeBook(name, …, appName)` passes the route's package-id segment, as the file's other reads do (`:64`, `:111`).
- **Clause-② widening.** `@objectstack/client`: `meta.getItems` options become the exported `MetaItemsListOptions` with an optional `include`, on both the unscoped and environment surfaces. Leaving it out sends nothing; a test pins the four URLs. The README line is added. The 13 new `@object-ui/i18n` keys are additive. `@object-ui/app-shell` is private: `AppHeaderVariant` gains `'docs'` and `HomeLayout` gains `variant`, and its three Record-keyed tests are updated. The changeset names all four packages, and its text matches the code sentence by sentence.
- **l1-face at 3f16d0bc: CLEAN.** 58 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending; floor checks green; mergeable_state clean. `Fixes #35424` is right: PR-a #36000 (merged) delivered items 1–5, and this PR delivers 6–9 and both acceptance lines.

### Owed

- S1, which I will read as a delta on a later head. The L1 is final on that head once green, or on this one if the seat declines S1.
- The L2 for the declaration face (client export, i18n keys) is the seat's. This L1 does not replace it.

## 席位核对 — delta ACCEPT (L1-b)

Head-sha: c81b902f61f5a53b6a72b7764ceecd9bb44de3d0 · read 2026-11-21T08:32Z · delta 3f16d0bc..c81b902f only (one commit, 3 files), on top of ACCEPT 7059942047.

### 维护者速读

- 上一轮提的那处已改好：搜索结果里的手册名现在和卡片上一致。中文界面下，系统设置的文章显示「系统设置」，不再显示英文「Setup」。
- 新加的测试覆盖了这个情况，并有对照。
- 没有别的改动。

### Must-fix / Should-fix

None. S1 from 7059942047 is closed.

### Checked

- **S1 closed.** `searchDocs` now takes `listedBooks: ReadonlyMap<book name, card label>`. The listing gate still reads `listedBooks.has(book.name)`, so the search still offers no article the page does not list. `bookLabel` is `listedBooks.get(book.name) ?? book.label ?? book.name`. `DocsIndex` builds the map from `groups`, the same cards the page draws, so an implicit book's hit carries its app's label. The new unit case runs `groupBooksByApp` and then `searchDocs`, and expects the Setup hit's book line to read 'System Settings'. Its control asserts the book's own label differs. The existing cases move from `Set` to `Map` with no change in what they assert.
- **Scope.** Only `docs-index.ts`, `DocsIndex.tsx` and `docs-index.test.ts` changed. No public surface, changeset or i18n changes.

### Owed

- CI green at c81b902f. The L1 is final on that green head.
- The declaration L2 is the seat's. This L1 does not replace it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `3f16d0bcd2f9bb41afdbbdeeb6dc8b751cb3e904`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (owed by the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line alone; the tree carries no published schema and no governed path). Inputs read: card #35424 (body and all four comments: the triage, the PR-a claim, its amendment, the PR-b claim), PR #36027 (body, 32-file list, net diff against main at merge-base 141a826f), and the 68 check-runs on the head: every one `success` or `skipped`, none failing or pending. Code outside the diff (the REST list chain, the Setup app, the MCP doc door) was read to judge the diff, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@objectstack/client` `meta.getItems(type, { include })`: right.** Both the unscoped surface (`ObjectStackClient.meta.getItems`) and the environment-scoped one (`ScopedEnvironmentClient.meta.getItems`) now send `?include=` when the option is set, and nothing when it is left out (the `client.test.ts` case pins all four URLs, including the no-option control). The server already accepts both values on the same list door, with no server change in this diff:
  - `include` is in the list's closed query set (`META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS`) and in its single-value arity set (`META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`), `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts`.
  - `'content'`: step 6 of `createMetaListAnswer` strips each doc's `content` unless `query.include === 'content'`.
  - `'grants'`: step 8 runs `describeMetaPositionList` on `position` only when `query.include === 'grants'` (#25333).
  - Same audience gate: both steps run after step 2, the per-caller list gate (`createMetaListReadGate`, the ADR-0046 §6.7 docs-audience arm). So `?include=content` serves bodies only for the docs the slim list already admits. Both transports (RestServer and the runtime dispatcher's twin) hand their list to this one function, and the environment-scoped mount registers the same handler. The PR body's "through the same audience gate as the list" is accurate.
  - The client's union `'content' | 'grants'` is exactly the two values the server acts on. Its jsdoc names the type each one applies to (`doc`, `position`); a value on another type is a no-op on the server, which is existing behaviour. The option is a REST-wire option: `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` in `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` declares no `include`, and none is needed for a transport parameter. No spec change.
- **`MetaItemsListOptions` exported from `@objectstack/client`: right.** It is a new named export from the package entry (`src/index.ts`). It replaces the inline `{ packageId?, names? }` with the same two members plus `include`, so no existing caller narrows. README line added.
- **`@object-ui/i18n` keys: right.** The diff adds nine base `help.*` keys: `docsIndexSubtitle`, `searchAllDocs`, `articleCount`, `otherDocs`, `noDocsInstalled`, `loadDocsFailed`, `searchingDocs`, `searchResultCount`, `docsSearchFailed`. Two of them (`articleCount`, `searchResultCount`) are plural, with per-locale CLDR forms (ar carries zero/one/two/few/many/other). All 11 packs are touched and no key is removed (the diff has zero `-` lines under `ui/packages/i18n`). This matches the declared "nine help.* keys (two of them plural)".
- **`@object-ui/app-shell` (`AppHeaderVariant` gains `docs`; `HomeLayout`/`DefaultHomeLayout` take `variant`): right, and not counted.** The package is `private: true`, so these are not published surface. This is consistent with the PR-a amendment's reading.
- **`@object-ui/console` routes: right, and disclosed.** `/docs` and its children move from a bare `ProtectedRoute` into Home's frame, under the organization and permissions layout. So the portal now needs an active organization, as `/home` does. The PR body says so ("under the same organization / permissions layout as `/home`"). This is not a published API.
- **Item 8 wording, code against text: right on the axis asked.** The code says "This is a listing rule, not a read gate: the server's audience gate (ADR-0046 §6.7) is what decides who may read a doc" (`groupBooksByApp` jsdoc, `docs-index.ts`). The PR body says "This is what the page lists, not who may read a doc", and the maintainer summary says 「这只是「列不列」，谁能读文档仍由服务端的受众规则决定」. The changeset repeats the PR body's sentence. Neither the code nor the text says "not readable" anywhere. The full-text search keeps to the same rule: `searchDocs` answers only articles whose home book is in `listedBooks`, which is pinned by "answers no article of a book the page does not list". The premise also holds on main: `SETUP_APP.requiredPermissions` is `['setup.access']` (`packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup.app.ts:47`), so `/meta/app` leaves Setup out for a member without it. See F2 for one precision gap in "listed only under its app".

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/35424-all-docs-page.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/client`, `@object-ui/console`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`. The diff has `Metadata-protocol: none` (no authorable key, value or type changes), and under AGENTS.md "Land it" rule 3 a `none` kind ships `patch`, widening included. **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: right. The diff publishes an optional `include` option and a new exported type on `@objectstack/client`, plus nine keys on `@object-ui/i18n`, and removes nothing from any published package. App-shell is private and correctly left off the line. The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset body, and each one is line-initial. The `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` check-runs are `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

The PR-b claim (card comment 7059265831) carries five readings. Here is how each is answered:

1. Item 9 search in the browser over `GET /meta/doc?include=content`: answered. The parameter exists and is gated as the claim says (see ①). The SQL judgment is under F3.
2. Item 8 "admins only" read as a listing rule: answered in the code and the text, which are consistent with each other (see ①). The claim's own residual is **not** escalated. See F1.
3. Item 7 grouping (first linking app in launcher order, else the package's app, else "Other documentation"; launcher names; no package id; plural counts): answered in code and pinned in `docs-index.test.ts` and `docs-portal.test.tsx`.
4. Item 6 header: answered. `DocShell` draws no bar off an app, and `AppHeader`'s `docs` variant is pinned in three AppHeader tests.
5. Notes carried from PR-a (N3 redirect, `bookHoldsArticle`, `backLink={!docsNav}`, the label differing from 「Search docs」): answered and pinned.

No `open_questions` entry is present on the card or the PR.

**SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** The full-text search fetches every listed doc's body into the browser once, on the first keystroke (`useDocContents`), and matches there. The reason given is in the claim's scope item 1 and the PR body: reuse the existing gated `?include=content` list, add no new REST route, and ask once, lazily, and keep the answer for the page's life. This is not an SQL-capable path being kept in the app. Docs are metadata items, merged from the package registry and the stored overlay and judged by the in-process per-caller gate before step 6. So the list door has no SQL query a search could be pushed into, and the diff adds no new id materialisation and no in-app join over SQL-backed rows. The line is not crossed. See F3 for what the stated reason leaves out.

**Findings**

- **F1, should-fix (③, flag not escalated).** The claim reads card item 8 (「系统包…只给管理员看」) as a listing rule, and says that "a server-side gate would need an audience-scoped book for Setup and is a separate card." No such card exists: an issue and PR search for 35424 finds only this card, #35981, #6015, this PR and #36000. The PR carries `Fixes #35424`, so merging it closes the card, and the residual would be named nowhere. On main, `SETUP_OVERVIEW_DOC` carries no audience. So for a member without `setup.access`, the Setup overview's body still arrives in the browser in this page's own `?include=content` answer, and it reads at its direct URL. The PR states this honestly as "not listed". But the maintainer's word on the card was "only admins see it", and the narrowing to a listing rule has been neither ruled on by the maintainer nor filed. Fix: file the follow-up card (an audience-scoped book or doc for Setup), or put the listing-only reading on #35424 for the maintainer's word, and link it from the PR body before merge.
- **F2, nit (① text against code).** The PR body and changeset say "A platform package's books (`com.objectstack.*`) are listed only under its app". `groupBooksByApp` actually assigns a book to the first app whose navigation links it, and only then to its package's app. A platform book never falls into "Other documentation", but a business app that links one would list it for a member who lacks the platform app. That is defensible, because such a member reaches it through that app's navigation anyway. But it is not what the text says, and no test pins it. Suggested wording: "listed only under an app in the member's list that carries it, never under Other documentation".
